items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: there was a certain girl, tall beautiful girl, but she was just tall and beautiful. Her name was Amy. Well, Amy could sing, she had a deep voice, you know, a contralto voice, but it was a pleasant voice, but she could sing beautifully.

ctx.x: Now, we had another boy named Wilson Miles, well, they swear that he was from there, and Wilson Miles was there about two weeks and he was on the corner talking to the cabdrivers. He was just talking as if he were a citizen of the place, so all right, we all got our pay and got all our money

and got all our ladyfriend, and there were some English people who followed us all around and there was a certain girl, tall beautiful girl, but she was just tall and beautiful. Her name was Amy. Well, Amy could sing, she had a deep voice, you know, a contralto voice, but it was a pleasant voice, but she could sing beautifully. Now, on the ship coming back, everybody's happy. I think Burns had a case full of — , of cocaine which was nothing to — about, just nothing, just — and everybody was happy.
We're all sitting on the deck and they said, Amy, go on and sing a song. Sing Ole' Man River, Amy. She said, I don't like that song, don't ask me to -- and they kept on bugging her.
